entities.name: Accounts
entities.text: A person who can sign in to the marketplace. Every account is exactly one of a customer, a staff member or a courier (see the ISA hierarchy).

entities.name: Customers
entities.text: An account that shops: it owns a cart, wishlists, saved payment methods and orders, and collects loyalty points.

entities.name: Staff
entities.text: An account that works for the marketplace or for sellers: verifies sellers, answers questions, inspects warehouses and returns. Every staff member belongs to one department.

entities.name: Couriers
entities.text: An account that delivers shipments. A courier holds a licence, may be assigned one vehicle and serves one or more delivery zones.

entities.name: Departments
entities.text: An internal unit of the marketplace (for example Seller Operations). It has a budget and at most one managing staff member.

entities.name: Loyalty_Tiers
entities.text: A level of the customer loyalty programme (Bronze, Silver, ...). A customer reaches a tier at a points threshold and receives its discount.

entities.name: Vehicles
entities.text: A fleet vehicle (bicycle, motorbike or van) with a carrying capacity. A vehicle is assigned to at most one courier at a time.

entities.name: Seller_Organizations
entities.text: An independent business that sells on the marketplace. It is owned by one account, pays commission under one plan and lists products.

entities.name: Commission_Plans
entities.text: A pricing plan that sets the commission percentage the marketplace keeps from a seller's sales.

entities.name: Seller_Verifications
entities.text: One onboarding check of a seller (identity, tax documents) with its outcome. A seller can be checked several times.

entities.name: Seller_Policies
entities.text: A versioned seller rule shown to buyers, such as a return or shipping policy, with the date it takes effect.

entities.name: Seller_Payout_Accounts
entities.text: A bank account (stored masked) into which a seller receives its earnings, with a verification status.

entities.name: Seller_Payouts
entities.text: One transfer of a seller's earnings for a settlement period into one payout account.

entities.name: Customer_Notifications
entities.text: A message sent to a customer (order shipped, price dropped) together with when it was read.
entities.why: A customer receives many notifications, each with its own read time.

entities.name: Countries
entities.text: A country the marketplace operates in, identified by its two-letter ISO code.
entities.why: Cities and tax rates both depend on the country; a separate entity stores the country name once.

entities.name: Cities
entities.text: A city inside a country. Addresses, warehouses, delivery zones and pickup points are located in cities.
entities.why: Addresses, warehouses, zones and pickup points all refer to cities, and we want to search by city. As the slide on addresses says, when the structure matters it must be an entity.

entities.name: Addresses
entities.text: A delivery address saved by an account, located in one city.

entities.name: Delivery_Zones
entities.text: A district of a city that couriers are assigned to serve.

entities.name: Pickup_Points
entities.text: A parcel locker or partner shop in a city where a customer may collect an order instead of home delivery.

entities.name: Tax_Rates
entities.text: A named sales-tax rate (for example Standard VAT 20%) defined by one country and applied to invoice lines.

entities.name: Categories
entities.text: A product classification. Categories form a tree: a category may have a parent category.

entities.name: Brands
entities.text: A manufacturer or brand name that labels products.

entities.name: Products
entities.text: A shared catalogue description of a product (name, text) that belongs to one category and one brand. Sellers sell its variants.

entities.name: Variants
entities.text: A concrete, stock-keeping version of a product (for example the black headphones), identified by its SKU.

entities.name: Product_Images
entities.text: A picture of a product with alternative text and a display position.
entities.why: A product has many images, each with its own URL, text and position. Attributes cannot be set-valued, so images are an entity set.

entities.name: Attributes
entities.text: A dimension along which variants differ, such as Color or Size.

entities.name: Listings
entities.text: One seller's priced offer of one variant. A seller can list a variant at most once.

entities.name: Price_History
entities.text: One recorded price change of a listing: the old price, the new price and when it changed.
entities.why: A listing changes price many times and each change has its own old price, new price and time. Storing only the current price would lose the history.

entities.name: Product_Questions
entities.text: A public question that a customer asks about a product.

entities.name: Product_Answers
entities.text: A staff member's answer to a product question.

entities.name: Product_Documents
entities.text: A downloadable file for a product, such as a manual or a warranty certificate.
entities.why: A product may have several documents of different types.

entities.name: Seller_Reviews
entities.text: A customer's star rating and comment about a seller (at most one per customer and seller).

entities.name: Carts
entities.text: The single shopping cart that a customer is currently filling.

entities.name: Wishlists
entities.text: A named list in which a customer saves listings for later.

entities.name: Promotions
entities.text: A time-limited discount campaign run by a seller.

entities.name: Coupons
entities.text: A code issued under a promotion that can be redeemed a limited number of times.

entities.name: Reviews
entities.text: A customer's star rating and comment about a product (at most one per customer and product).

entities.name: Review_Images
entities.text: A photo attached to a product review.
entities.why: A review can carry several photos, so the photos cannot be a single-valued attribute of the review.

entities.name: Gift_Cards
entities.text: A prepaid card bought by a customer, with a code, an initial value and a remaining balance.

entities.name: Warehouses
entities.text: A fulfilment centre in a city where sellers keep stock.

entities.name: Storage_Bins
entities.text: A shelf location in a warehouse where stock batches are placed. Its address is a zone code and a shelf code (for example zone A, shelf A-01), unique within the warehouse.

entities.name: Stock_Batches
entities.text: A physical quantity of one stock position received at one time and stored in one bin. Batches let the system issue the oldest stock first.

entities.name: Stock_Movements
entities.text: A signed change of a batch's quantity with its reason: made by the system (an order reservation) or entered by hand after a count or damage, then authorised by a staff member.
entities.why: A batch changes many times and each change must be auditable with its reason and time.

entities.name: Suppliers
entities.text: A wholesaler from which a seller buys goods.

entities.name: Purchase_Orders
entities.text: An order a seller places with a supplier for delivery to one warehouse.

entities.name: Purchase_Order_Lines
entities.text: One line of a purchase order: which variant, how many and at what unit cost. Numbered within its purchase order.

entities.name: Goods_Receipts
entities.text: The record of a delivery arriving at the warehouse against a purchase order. One purchase order may arrive in several deliveries.

entities.name: Warehouse_Inspections
entities.text: A safety or quality inspection of a warehouse performed by a staff member, with its result.

entities.name: Orders
entities.text: A customer's purchase of one or more listings, delivered to an address or a pickup point, with its status and total.

entities.name: Order_Lines
entities.text: One line of an order: which listing, how many and the unit price at checkout. Numbered within its order.

entities.name: Order_Status_Events
entities.text: One step in an order's history (placed, shipped, delivered) with its time.
entities.why: An order passes through several statuses and we want the time of each. A single status attribute keeps only the latest one.

entities.name: Payment_Methods
entities.text: A card, wallet or bank account a customer has saved for paying (stored masked).

entities.name: Payments
entities.text: The payment of one order, made with one payment method, with its amount and status.

entities.name: Payment_Transactions
entities.text: One money movement of a payment: the capture, or a refund paid back for an approved return request.
entities.why: One payment produces several money movements over time (capture, later refunds).

entities.name: Invoices
entities.text: The legal invoice issued for an order.

entities.name: Invoice_Lines
entities.text: One line of an invoice: the billed amount for one order line and the tax rate applied. Numbered within its invoice.

entities.name: Fulfillments
entities.text: The part of an order that one seller prepares from one warehouse. A multi-seller order is split into several fulfilments.

entities.name: Packages
entities.text: A physical parcel packed for a fulfilment, with its weight.

entities.name: Carriers
entities.text: A shipping company that transports packages.

entities.name: Carrier_Services
entities.text: A delivery service offered by a carrier (Standard, Express) with its maximum delivery time. The service code is only unique within its carrier.

entities.name: Shipments
entities.text: The transport of one package with one carrier service, identified by a tracking code.

entities.name: Tracking_Events
entities.text: One scan of a shipment along its route: status, location and time.
entities.why: A shipment is scanned many times, each scan with a location and time.

entities.name: Delivery_Attempts
entities.text: One try by a courier to hand over a shipment, with its outcome. A successful attempt also records the proof of delivery: who received the parcel and, optionally, a photo or signature link; these attributes stay empty on failed attempts. A shipment can fail several times but is delivered at most once.

entities.name: Return_Requests
entities.text: A customer's request to send back items of a delivered order, with the reason and its status.

entities.name: Return_Inspections
entities.text: The check of returned goods by a staff member before they may be restocked.

entities.name: Support_Tickets
entities.text: A help request opened by a customer, optionally about a specific order.

entities.name: Ticket_Messages
entities.text: One message in a support ticket's conversation, written by an account.
entities.why: A ticket holds a conversation of many messages, each with its own author, which is itself a relationship to Accounts.

relationships.name: Belongs_To
relationships.text: A customer belongs to at most one loyalty tier (none before the first purchase); a tier has many customers.

relationships.name: Works_In
relationships.text: Every staff member works in exactly one department; a department has many staff.

relationships.name: Drives
relationships.text: One-to-one: a courier drives at most one vehicle and a vehicle is assigned to at most one courier. Both sides are optional.

relationships.name: Manages
relationships.text: A department is managed by at most one staff member (the same Manages example as the Key Constraints slide). Not every department needs a manager, so participation is partial.

relationships.name: Subscribes_To
relationships.text: Every seller is on exactly one commission plan; a plan has many sellers.

relationships.name: Owns
relationships.text: Every seller is owned by exactly one account; one person may own several sellers.

relationships.name: Checks
relationships.text: A staff member checks verifications. A verification that is still pending has no checker yet, so the Verification side is partial.

relationships.name: Verification_Of
relationships.text: Each verification is about exactly one seller; a seller can be verified several times.

relationships.name: Publishes
relationships.text: Each policy is published by exactly one seller.

relationships.name: Paid_Into
relationships.text: Each payout account belongs to exactly one seller; a seller may register several.

relationships.name: Pays_To
relationships.text: Each payout is transferred to exactly one payout account.

relationships.name: Notifies
relationships.text: Each notification is sent to exactly one customer.

relationships.name: Part_Of
relationships.text: Each city is part of exactly one country; a country has many cities.

relationships.name: Lies_In
relationships.text: Each address lies in exactly one city.

relationships.name: Saves_Address
relationships.text: Each address is saved by exactly one account; an account can save many addresses.
rules: An order is billed to an address that its own customer saved (together with Places and Billed_To); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Zone_Of
relationships.text: Each delivery zone lies in exactly one city; a city may be divided into several zones.

relationships.name: Placed_In
relationships.text: Each pickup point is in exactly one city.

relationships.name: Levied_By
relationships.text: Each tax rate is defined by exactly one country; a country defines several rates.

relationships.name: Subcategory_Of
relationships.text: A category may have one parent category; a parent has many subcategories. The same entity set appears in two roles, as in the Reports_To example.

relationships.name: Made_By
relationships.text: Every product is made by exactly one brand.

relationships.name: Classified_As
relationships.text: Every product is classified under exactly one category.

relationships.name: Variant_Of
relationships.text: Every variant is a version of exactly one product; a product has at least one variant.

relationships.name: Illustrates
relationships.text: Each image illustrates exactly one product.

relationships.name: Lists
relationships.text: Each listing sells exactly one variant; a variant can be listed by several sellers.

relationships.name: Offers
relationships.text: Each listing is offered by exactly one seller.

relationships.name: Price_Change_Of
relationships.text: Each price change belongs to exactly one listing.

relationships.name: Asks
relationships.text: Each question is asked by exactly one customer.

relationships.name: Asked_About
relationships.text: Each question is about exactly one product.

relationships.name: Writes_Answer
relationships.text: Each answer is written by exactly one staff member.

relationships.name: Answers
relationships.text: Each answer replies to exactly one question; a question may get several answers.

relationships.name: Documents
relationships.text: Each document belongs to exactly one product.

relationships.name: Writes_Seller_Review
relationships.text: Each seller review is written by exactly one customer.

relationships.name: Reviews_Seller
relationships.text: Each seller review is about exactly one seller.

relationships.name: Has_Cart
relationships.text: One-to-one: every cart belongs to exactly one customer and a customer has at most one cart.

relationships.name: Keeps
relationships.text: Each wishlist is kept by exactly one customer.

relationships.name: Runs
relationships.text: Each promotion is run by exactly one seller.

relationships.name: Issues
relationships.text: Each coupon is issued under exactly one promotion.

relationships.name: Writes_Review
relationships.text: Each review is written by exactly one customer.

relationships.name: Reviews_Product
relationships.text: Each review is about exactly one product.

relationships.name: Attached_To
relationships.text: Each review image is attached to exactly one review.

relationships.name: Buys_Gift_Card
relationships.text: Each gift card is bought by exactly one customer.

relationships.name: Sited_In
relationships.text: Each warehouse is sited in exactly one city.

relationships.name: Located_In
relationships.text: Each bin is in exactly one warehouse; a warehouse has many bins.

relationships.name: Stored_In
relationships.text: Each batch is stored in exactly one bin, and the bin must be in the batch's own warehouse.
rules: A stock batch is stored in a bin of its own warehouse (together with Batch_Of); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Batch_Of
relationships.text: Each batch belongs to exactly one stock position, that is, to one Stocks relationship (aggregation). A stock position consists of many batches.
relationships.sql: foreign key stock_batches(seller_id, variant_id, warehouse_id) → stock_positions
rules: A stock batch is stored in a bin of its own warehouse (together with Stored_In); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Authorizes
relationships.text: A manual movement (a count correction or damage) is authorised by one staff member; movements made by the system, such as order reservations, have none.

relationships.name: Moves
relationships.text: Each movement changes exactly one batch.

relationships.name: Uses_Supplier
relationships.text: Each supplier record belongs to exactly one seller.

relationships.name: Delivered_To
relationships.text: Each purchase order is delivered to exactly one warehouse.

relationships.name: Ordered_From
relationships.text: Each purchase order is placed with exactly one supplier.

relationships.name: Orders_Variant
relationships.text: Each purchase-order line orders exactly one variant.

relationships.name: PO_Has_Line
relationships.kind: identifying relationship of a weak entity (one owner, many weak entities)
relationships.text: A purchase-order line exists only inside its purchase order and is numbered within it.

relationships.name: Receipt_For
relationships.text: Each goods receipt is for exactly one purchase order.
rules: A goods receipt only receives lines of its own purchase order (together with Receives); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Conducts
relationships.text: Each inspection is conducted by exactly one staff member.

relationships.name: Inspects
relationships.text: Each inspection is of exactly one warehouse.

relationships.name: Collect_At
relationships.text: An order may be collected at one pickup point instead of being delivered to its address.

relationships.name: Billed_To
relationships.text: Every order has exactly one billing address, and the VAT rate comes from its country. A home-delivery order is also shipped to this address; a pickup order is collected at its pickup point (Collect_At).
rules: An order is billed to an address that its own customer saved (together with Places and Saves_Address); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Places
relationships.text: Every order is placed by exactly one customer.
rules: An order is billed to an address that its own customer saved (together with Billed_To and Saves_Address); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key
A support ticket can only be about an order of the customer who opened it (together with Opens and About_Order); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Buys
relationships.text: Each order line buys exactly one listing.

relationships.name: Contains
relationships.kind: identifying relationship of a weak entity (one owner, many weak entities)
relationships.text: An order line exists only inside its order and is numbered within it. Every order has at least one line.

relationships.name: Status_Of
relationships.text: Each status event belongs to exactly one order.

relationships.name: Saves_Method
relationships.text: Each payment method is saved by exactly one customer.
rules: An order is paid with a payment method that its own customer saved (together with Paid_By and Uses_Method); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Uses_Method
relationships.text: Every payment uses exactly one saved payment method.
rules: An order is paid with a payment method that its own customer saved (together with Paid_By and Saves_Method); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Paid_By
relationships.text: One-to-one: every payment is for exactly one order and an order has at most one payment.
rules: An order is paid with a payment method that its own customer saved (together with Uses_Method and Saves_Method); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Refund_For
relationships.text: A refund transaction pays back exactly one return request; capture transactions belong to no return.
rules: A refund is paid back from the payment of the order that was returned (together with Transaction_Of); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Transaction_Of
relationships.text: Each transaction belongs to exactly one payment.
rules: A refund is paid back from the payment of the order that was returned (together with Refund_For); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Invoiced_As
relationships.text: One-to-one: every invoice is for exactly one order and an order has at most one invoice.
rules: An invoice only bills lines of its own order (together with Invoice_Has_Line and Bills); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Bills
relationships.text: Each invoice line bills exactly one order line.
rules: An invoice only bills lines of its own order (together with Invoiced_As and Invoice_Has_Line); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Taxed_At
relationships.text: An invoice line is taxed at most at one tax rate (none for tax-exempt lines).

relationships.name: Invoice_Has_Line
relationships.kind: identifying relationship of a weak entity (one owner, many weak entities)
relationships.text: An invoice line exists only inside its invoice and is numbered within it.
rules: An invoice only bills lines of its own order (together with Invoiced_As and Bills); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Picked_From
relationships.text: Each fulfilment is picked from exactly one warehouse.

relationships.name: Handled_By
relationships.text: Each fulfilment is handled by exactly one seller.

relationships.name: Fulfills
relationships.text: Each fulfilment fulfils exactly one order.
rules: A fulfilment only includes lines of its own order (together with Includes); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Packed_For
relationships.text: Each package is packed for exactly one fulfilment.

relationships.name: Offers_Service
relationships.kind: identifying relationship of a weak entity (one owner, many weak entities)
relationships.text: A carrier service exists only for its carrier; the service code (STD, EXP) is unique only within the carrier. Every carrier offers at least one service.

relationships.name: Ships_Via
relationships.text: Every shipment travels with exactly one carrier service.

relationships.name: Ships
relationships.text: One-to-one: every shipment carries exactly one package and a package is shipped at most once.

relationships.name: Tracks
relationships.text: Each tracking event is for exactly one shipment.

relationships.name: Makes_Attempt
relationships.text: Each delivery attempt is made by exactly one courier.

relationships.name: Attempts
relationships.text: Each delivery attempt is for exactly one shipment.

relationships.name: Return_Of
relationships.text: Each return request is for exactly one order. The customer is reached through the order.
rules: A return request only returns lines of its own order (together with Returns); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Inspects_Return
relationships.text: Each return inspection is done by exactly one staff member.

relationships.name: Inspection_Of
relationships.text: Each inspection checks exactly one return request.

relationships.name: About_Order
relationships.text: A ticket may be about one order.
rules: A support ticket can only be about an order of the customer who opened it (together with Opens and Places); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Opens
relationships.text: Each ticket is opened by exactly one customer.
rules: A support ticket can only be about an order of the customer who opened it (together with About_Order and Places); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Writes_Message
relationships.text: Each message is written by exactly one account (customer or staff).

relationships.name: Message_In
relationships.text: Each message belongs to exactly one ticket.

relationships.name: Employs
relationships.text: A seller employs staff members to run its shop; a staff member may work for several sellers. The relationship records when the assignment started.

relationships.name: Serves
relationships.text: A courier serves one or more delivery zones and a zone is served by several couriers, each since a given date.

relationships.name: Has_Value
relationships.text: A variant has a value for an attribute (Color = Black). The value belongs to the pair, not to either side alone.

relationships.name: In_Cart
relationships.text: A cart contains listings, each with a quantity. A listing can be in many customers' carts.

relationships.name: Saved_In
relationships.text: A wishlist holds listings, and the same listing may be saved in many wishlists.

relationships.name: Redeems
relationships.text: An order redeems coupons. A coupon can be used by several orders up to its limit, and an order may use several coupons. The customer is not stored again because it is the customer of the order.

relationships.name: Pays_With
relationships.text: An order is partly paid with gift cards; the relationship records how much of each card was spent.

relationships.name: Stocks
relationships.text: A seller stocks a variant in a warehouse, with the available quantity and a reorder point. The quantity belongs to the triple: knowing that a seller sells a variant, that the seller uses a warehouse and that the warehouse holds the variant does not tell how many units of that seller's variant are in that warehouse (the Contracts argument on the Binary vs. Ternary slide).
relationships.sql: table stock_positions (primary key seller_id, variant_id, warehouse_id)

relationships.name: Receives
relationships.text: A goods receipt receives some quantity of purchase-order lines. A line can arrive across several receipts.
relationships.sql: table goods_receipt_lines (primary key receipt_id, purchase_order_id, line_no)
rules: A goods receipt only receives lines of its own purchase order (together with Receipt_For); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Reserves
relationships.text: An order line reserves a quantity from a stock position, that is, from a Stocks relationship (seller, variant, warehouse) treated as one object. One line may be served from several warehouses; the reserved quantities of a line add up to its ordered quantity.
relationships.sql: table stock_reservations (primary key order_id, line_no, seller_id, variant_id, warehouse_id)

relationships.name: Includes
relationships.text: A fulfilment includes some quantity of order lines; a line split across warehouses appears in several fulfilments.
relationships.sql: table fulfillment_lines (primary key fulfillment_id, order_id, line_no)
rules: A fulfilment only includes lines of its own order (together with Fulfills); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

relationships.name: Returns
relationships.text: A return request returns some quantity of order lines.
relationships.sql: table return_lines (primary key return_id, order_id, line_no)
rules: A return request only returns lines of its own order (together with Return_Of); the schema enforces it with a composite foreign key

isa.text: Customers, staff and couriers share the attributes of an account (e-mail, name) and inherit its key account_id, but each has its own attributes and takes part in different relationships. Overlap is not allowed: an account has exactly one role, and triggers reject a subtype row whose account has a different role. Covering holds: role is mandatory, so every account is one of the three.

total_participation.reason: checkout always creates at least one order line
a purchase order is created together with its lines
an invoice is issued with one line per order line
a product is only published with at least one variant
a carrier is only usable with at least one service
a courier is registered together with at least one delivery zone
checkout reserves stock for every order line and creates no order when stock is short
a fulfilment is created together with the order lines it ships
a return request is created together with the order lines it returns

cross_rules.rule: a goods receipt only receives lines of its own purchase order
cross_rules.how: goods_receipt_lines(receipt_id, purchase_order_id) references goods_receipts(receipt_id, purchase_order_id), and (purchase_order_id, line_no) references the purchase-order line, so both must name the same purchase order

cross_rules.rule: a return request only returns lines of its own order
cross_rules.how: return_lines(return_id, order_id) references return_requests(return_id, order_id), and (order_id, line_no) references the order line, so both must name the same order

cross_rules.rule: a refund is paid back from the payment of the order that was returned
cross_rules.how: payment_transactions carries order_id only for this: (payment_id, order_id) references payments and (return_id, order_id) references return_requests, so the payment and the return belong to the same order

cross_rules.rule: an order is billed to an address that its own customer saved
an order is paid with a payment method that its own customer saved
cross_rules.how: payments carries customer_id only for this: (order_id, customer_id) references orders and (payment_method_id, customer_id) references payment_methods, so the order and the method belong to the same customer

cross_rules.rule: an invoice only bills lines of its own order
cross_rules.how: invoice_lines(invoice_id, order_id) references invoices(invoice_id, order_id), and (order_id, order_line_no) references the order line, so both must name the same order

cross_rules.rule: a fulfilment only includes lines of its own order
cross_rules.how: fulfillment_lines(fulfillment_id, order_id) references fulfillments(fulfillment_id, order_id), and (order_id, line_no) references the order line, so both must name the same order

cross_rules.rule: a support ticket can only be about an order of the customer who opened it
a stock batch is stored in a bin of its own warehouse
cross_rules.how: stock_batches(bin_id, warehouse_id) references storage_bins(bin_id, warehouse_id), and warehouse_id is also part of the batch's stock position

checks.evidence: 67 entity sets, 99 relationship sets and the ISA hierarchy form one connected component

Order_Lines (owner Orders), Purchase_Order_Lines (owner Purchase_Orders), Invoice_Lines (owner Invoices), Carrier_Services (owner Carriers); each has a partial key and total participation with a key constraint in its identifying relationship
Accounts ISA Customers, Staff, Couriers (overlap: not allowed, covering: yes)
Stocks is aggregated; used by Batch_Of, Reserves

checks.requirement: 4. Every entity has a clearly defined key
checks.evidence: own key underlined for strong entity sets, partial key (dashed) + owner key for weak ones, key inherited from Accounts for subclasses
